title: Compatible finite quotient grid from adic formal smoothness
statement: Let R,S,A be commutative rings with R-algebra structures on S and A [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and n an ideal of S such that S is formally smooth over R for the n-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Let I,J be ideals of A and g:S -> A/J an R-algebra map satisfying g(n^r) contained in the image of I for some r≥1. There exist R-algebra maps F_{a,b}:S -> A/(J^a+I^b) for every a,b≥0, compatible with every quotient transition when a≤a′,b≤b′, such that F_{1,b} is g followed by A/J -> A/(J+I^b). No completeness or closedness is assumed, nor any containment of a power of J in I.

source.place: Proof of Lemma Tag 07NJ (lemma-lift-continuous), quotient grid and induction paragraphs; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NJ

proof.text: For every positive b, the first-row reduction of g annihilates n^(r*b): map the ideal n^r under g, take bth powers using map_pow and pow_mul, and then apply the quotient map, which kills the image of I^b. This is proved as the private lemma first_row_kills_power.

Use stages T(k) consisting of maps to A/(J^(k+1)+I^(k+1)) together with positive-power annihilation and the prescribed reduction to A/(J+I^(k+1)). The base stage is g reduced modulo J+I. Apply the one-step diagonal lemma with the next first-row reduction of g to extend each stage, preserving reduction to the previous stage. Quotient factor composition supplies compatibility of the inputs.

A proved dependent Nat-recursion lemma constructs a tower of stages from the base and the successor existence. Induction on the inequality between indices upgrades adjacent transition compatibility to every diagonal transition. Only theorem-level existence uses choice; no public definition selects arbitrary data from an existence theorem.

Define F(a,b) by projecting the tower entry at index max(a,b), whose diagonal exponent is max(a,b)+1. Monotonicity of max and quotient factor composition prove all two-index transition compatibilities. Project the prescribed first-row equation at the same diagonal index to prove the first-row identity. This also handles a=0 or b=0 directly; no separate zero-ring extension is needed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07NJ finite quotient-grid argument, replaced below the unit level by the cofinal diagonal tower; one-step diagonal variant and Lean recursion/projection proof written by F2.

lean.statement:
theorem FormallySmoothAdic.exists_quotient_grid
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {A : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing A] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R A]
    (n : Ideal S) (hS : FormallySmoothAdic R S n) (I J : Ideal A)
    (g : S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ J) (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (hg : ∀ x ∈ n ^ r, g x ∈ I.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)) :
    ∃ F : (a b : ℕ) → S →ₐ[R] A ⧸ (J ^ a ⊔ I ^ b),
      (∀ (a b a' b' : ℕ) (ha : a ≤ a') (hb : b ≤ b'),
        (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R (sup_le_sup
          (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right ha) (Ideal.pow_le_pow_right hb))).comp
            (F a' b') = F a b) ∧
      ∀ b : ℕ,
        (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R (show J ^ 1 ⊔ I ^ b ≤ J ⊔ I ^ b by simp)).comp
          (F 1 b) = (Ideal.Quotient.factorₐ R (le_sup_left : J ≤ J ⊔ I ^ b)).comp
            g
